title.zh: 第二十八 百官五 州郡 縣鄉 亭里 匈奴中郎將 烏桓校尉 護羌校尉 王國 宋衛國 列侯 關內侯 四夷國 百官奉
title.raw: 第二十八 百官五 州郡 縣鄉 亭里 匈奴中郎將 烏桓校尉 護羌校尉 王國 宋衛國 列侯 關內侯 四夷國 百官奉 Volume 118: Officials Part Five

sentences.zh: 志第二十八 百官五

translations.literal: Treatise number twenty-eight: Officials, part five.
translations.idiomatic: Monograph 28: The fifth installment on the bureaucracy of state.

sentences.zh: 州郡 县乡 亭里 匈奴中郎将 乌桓校尉 护羌校尉 王国 宋卫国 列侯 关内侯 四夷国 百官奉

translations.literal: Provinces and commanderies; counties and townships; wards and hamlets; Herald to the Xiongnu; Protector of the Wuhuan; Protector of the Qiang; princely kingdoms; the fiefs of Song and Wei; full marquisates; marquisates-within-the-passes; states of the four quarters; salaries of officials.
translations.idiomatic: Provinces and commanderies, counties and rural townships, wards and hamlets, the Herald to the Xiongnu, the Protector of the Wuhuan, the Protector of the Qiang, princely kingdoms, the domains of Song and Wei, full marquisates and marquisates-within-the-passes, tributary states beyond the inner realm, and the stipends paid to officials.

sentences.zh: 外十二州，每州刺史一人，六百石。

translations.literal: Outside the capital there were twelve provinces; each province had one inspector, at six hundred piculs.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond the metropolitan region lay twelve provinces, each overseen by a single regional inspector at the six-hundred-picul grade.

sentences.zh: 本注曰：秦有监御史，监诸郡，汉兴省之，但遣丞相史分刺诸州，无常官。

translations.literal: The original commentary says: The Qin had supervising clerks who oversaw the commanderies; when the Han arose they abolished them, and only sent out clerks from the chancellor’s office to investigate the provinces in rotation, without a permanent post.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: Under the Qin, supervising clerks watched over the commanderies; the Han at first abolished the office and merely dispatched secretaries from the chancellor’s staff on rotating inspections of the provinces, with no standing appointment.

sentences.zh: 孝武帝初置刺史十三人，秩六百石。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu at first established thirteen inspectors, rank six hundred piculs.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu initially appointed thirteen regional inspectors, each at the six-hundred-picul salary level.

sentences.zh: 成帝更为牧，秩二千石。

translations.literal: Emperor Cheng changed them to shepherds, rank two thousand piculs.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Cheng the title was changed to regional shepherd, with pay raised to two thousand piculs.

sentences.zh: 建武十八年，复为刺史，十二人各主一州，其一州属司隶校尉。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year of Jianwu they were again made inspectors, twelve men each in charge of one province; one province belonged to the Colonel Director of Retainers.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianwu 18 the office reverted to inspector; twelve men each governed one province, while the remaining province fell under the Colonel Director of Retainers at the capital.

sentences.zh: 诸州常以八月巡行所部郡国，录囚徒，考殿最。

translations.literal: The provinces regularly in the eighth month toured the commanderies and kingdoms under their jurisdiction, reviewing prisoners and assessing best and worst performance.
translations.idiomatic: Each province customarily made an autumn circuit of its commanderies and kingdoms, examining jail populations and rating administrative performance.

sentences.zh: 初岁尽诣京都奏事，中兴但因计吏。

translations.literal: At first at year’s end they went to the capital to report; in the restoration they relied only on the clerks who presented the annual accounts.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, inspectors had journeyed to the capital at year’s end to deliver their reports; after the restoration this duty devolved on the accounting clerks who came up with the tribute tallies.

sentences.zh: 皆有从事史、假佐。

translations.literal: All had attendant clerks and acting assistants.
translations.idiomatic: Each staff included attendant secretaries and provisional aides.

sentences.zh: 本注曰：员职略与司隶同，无都官从事，其功曹从事为治中从事。

translations.literal: The original commentary says: The posts were broadly the same as under the Colonel Director of Retainers, but without a capital-crimes attendant; the merit-clerk attendant was called the attendant for internal administration.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: The complement mirrored that of the Colonel Director of Retainers, except that there was no attendant for capital cases; the merit-clerk attendant was titled attendant for internal administration.

sentences.zh: 豫州部郡国六，冀州部九，兗州部八，徐州部五，青州部六，荆州部七，扬州部六，益州部十二，凉州部十二，并州部九，幽州部十一，交州部七，凡九十八。

translations.literal: Yuzhou supervised six commanderies and kingdoms; Jizhou nine; Yanzhou eight; Xuzhou five; Qingzhou six; Jingzhou seven; Yangzhou six; Yizhou twelve; Liangzhou twelve; Bingzhou nine; Youzhou eleven; Jiaozhou seven; in all ninety-eight.
translations.idiomatic: Yuzhou oversaw six commanderies and kingdoms; Jizhou nine; Yanzhou eight; Xuzhou five; Qingzhou six; Jingzhou seven; Yangzhou six; Yizhou twelve; Liangzhou twelve; Bingzhou nine; Youzhou eleven; Jiaozhou seven—ninety-eight units in all.

sentences.zh: 其二十七王国相，其七十一郡太守。

translations.literal: Of these twenty-seven were chancellors of princely kingdoms; seventy-one were grand administrators of commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-seven were chancellors serving princely fiefs; seventy-one were grand administrators of ordinary commanderies.

sentences.zh: 其属国都尉。

translations.literal: There were also chief commandants of dependent states.
translations.idiomatic: Dependent states were headed by chief commandants as well.

sentences.zh: 属国，分郡离远县置之，如郡差小，置本郡名。

translations.literal: Dependent states were set up by splitting off remote counties from a commandery; they were slightly smaller than a commandery and kept the parent commandery’s name.
translations.idiomatic: A dependent state was carved from outlying counties of a commandery; it was somewhat smaller than a full commandery and usually retained the original commandery designation.

sentences.zh: 世祖并省郡县四百余所，后世稍复增之。

translations.literal: Emperor Guangwu merged and abolished more than four hundred commanderies and counties; later ages gradually restored some.
translations.idiomatic: The founding emperor merged away over four hundred commanderies and counties; succeeding reigns slowly added others back.

sentences.zh: 凡州所监都为京都，置尹一人，二千石，丞一人，每郡置太守一人，二千石，丞一人。

translations.literal: In general, wherever a province supervised the capital district as its metropolis, one intendant was appointed at two thousand piculs and one assistant; each commandery had one grand administrator at two thousand piculs and one assistant.
translations.idiomatic: Where a province’s seat of supervision was the capital region, a single metropolitan intendant at two thousand piculs and one deputy were appointed; elsewhere each commandery had one grand administrator at two thousand piculs and one assistant.

sentences.zh: 郡当边戍者，丞为长史。

translations.literal: Commanderies on the frontier for garrison duty made the assistant a chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: On border commanderies charged with defense, the assistant was redesignated chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 王国之相亦如之。

translations.literal: The chancellors of princely kingdoms were the same.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellors of princely kingdoms followed the same rule.

sentences.zh: 每属国置都尉一人，比二千石，丞一人。

translations.literal: Each dependent state had one chief commandant, comparable to two thousand piculs, and one assistant.
translations.idiomatic: Each dependent state placed one chief commandant at the “comparable to two thousand piculs” grade, plus a single assistant.

sentences.zh: 本注曰：凡郡国皆掌治民，进贤劝功，决讼检奸。

translations.literal: The original commentary says: In general commanderies and kingdoms governed the people, advanced the worthy, urged achievement, decided lawsuits, and checked wrongdoing.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: Commanderies and kingdoms were responsible for governing the populace, recommending talent, encouraging good service, adjudicating litigation, and suppressing crime.

sentences.zh: 常以春行所主县，劝民农桑，振救乏绝。

translations.literal: They regularly in spring toured the counties under their charge, urging farming and sericulture, and relieving those in want.
translations.idiomatic: Each spring they made a circuit of subordinate counties to promote agriculture and silk production and to aid the destitute.

sentences.zh: 秋冬遣无害吏案讯诸囚，平其罪法，论课殿最。

translations.literal: In autumn and winter they sent harmless clerks to interrogate all prisoners, balance penalties according to law, and assess best and worst.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn and winter they dispatched incorruptible subordinates to review prisoners, align sentences with the code, and grade performance.

sentences.zh: 岁尽遣吏上计。

translations.literal: At year’s end they sent clerks up with the annual accounts.
translations.idiomatic: At the close of the year clerks carried the annual accounts to their superiors.

sentences.zh: 并举孝廉，郡口二十万举一人。

translations.literal: They also recommended filial and incorrupt candidates; for every two hundred thousand mouths in the commandery one man was recommended.
translations.idiomatic: They nominated candidates for the filial-and-incorrupt quota at the rate of one man per two hundred thousand registered persons.

sentences.zh: 尉一人，典兵禁，备盗贼，景帝更名都尉。

translations.literal: One commandant, in charge of troops and prohibitions, guarding against bandits; Emperor Jing changed the name to commandant.
translations.idiomatic: A commandant oversaw military readiness and police functions; Emperor Jing renamed the post commandant of the commandery.

sentences.zh: 武帝又置三辅都尉各一人，讥出入。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu also placed one metropolitan commandant in each of the three adjunct capitals, to regulate entry and exit.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu further assigned one commandant to each of the three capital adjuncts to control traffic in and out of those regions.

sentences.zh: 边郡置农都尉，主屯田殖谷。

translations.literal: Border commanderies set agricultural commandants in charge of garrison fields and grain increase.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier commanderies appointed agricultural commandants to manage military colonies and grain production.

sentences.zh: 又置属国都尉，主蛮夷降者。

translations.literal: They also set chief commandants of dependent states in charge of surrendered barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Chief commandants of dependent states were added to administer surrendered non-Chinese peoples.

sentences.zh: 中兴建武六年，省诸郡都尉，并职太守，无都试之役。

translations.literal: In the restoration, the sixth year of Jianwu, all commandery commandants were abolished and their duties merged with the grand administrator; there were no more general musters.
translations.idiomatic: After the restoration, in Jianwu 6, commandery-level commandants were eliminated and their powers folded into the grand administrator’s office, ending the empire-wide autumn drills.

sentences.zh: 省关都尉，唯边郡往往置都尉及属国都尉，稍有分县，治民比郡。

translations.literal: The pass commandants were abolished; only border commanderies commonly retained commandants and chief commandants of dependent states, sometimes with divided counties, governing people on a par with a commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Interior pass commandants were dropped; frontier areas often kept commandants and dependent-state commandants, sometimes with split counties whose magistrates ruled populations comparable to a full commandery.

sentences.zh: 安帝以羌犯法，三辅有陵园之守，乃复置右扶风都尉，京兆虎牙都尉。

translations.literal: Emperor An, because the Qiang broke the law and the three adjuncts guarded imperial tombs, again set a commandant of Right Fufeng and a “tiger-teeth” commandant of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qiang revolted and the three adjuncts had to secure the imperial mausolea, Emperor An restored the Right Fufeng commandant and the Jingzhao “tiger-teeth” commandant.

sentences.zh: 皆置诸曹掾史。

translations.literal: All established various bureau clerks and secretaries.
translations.idiomatic: Each administration staffed the usual bureaus with clerks and secretaries.

sentences.zh: 本注曰：诸曹略如公府曹，无东西曹。

translations.literal: The original commentary says: The bureaus were roughly like those of the Excellencies’ offices, but without east and west bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: The bureau system paralleled the central ministries, minus the eastern and western personnel offices.

sentences.zh: 有功曹史，主选署功劳。

translations.literal: There was a merit-clerk secretary in charge of appointments and recording merit.
translations.idiomatic: A merit-clerk secretary handled selections and service records.

sentences.zh: 有五官掾，署功曹及诸曹事。

translations.literal: There was a steward of the five bureaus who supervised the merit clerk and the other bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: A steward of the five bureaus oversaw the merit office and the remaining bureaus.

sentences.zh: 其监属县，有五部督邮，曹掾一人。

translations.literal: For supervision of subordinate counties there were five route inspectors, one bureau clerk each.
translations.idiomatic: Five route inspectors watched the dependent counties, each supported by a bureau clerk.

sentences.zh: 正门有亭长一人。

translations.literal: At the main gate there was one ward head.
translations.idiomatic: The main gate was guarded by a single ward head.

sentences.zh: 主记室史，主录记书，催期会。

translations.literal: A master of records in charge of copying documents and urging deadlines.
translations.idiomatic: The master of records maintained correspondence and enforced meeting schedules.

sentences.zh: 无令史。

translations.literal: There were no order-clerks.
translations.idiomatic: The post of order-clerk was omitted.

sentences.zh: 阁下及诸曹各有书佐，干主文书。

translations.literal: Below the pavilion gate and in each bureau there were document assistants who managed paperwork.
translations.idiomatic: Under the gate and in every bureau document assistants handled the written work.

sentences.zh: 属官，每县、邑、道，大者置令一人，千石：其次置长，四百石；

translations.literal: Subordinate offices: for each county, town, or circuit, the largest had one magistrate at one thousand piculs;
translations.idiomatic: Below them, each county, noble town, or barbarian circuit of the first rank had a magistrate at one thousand piculs;

sentences.zh: 小者置长，三百石；

translations.literal: the next size had a chief at four hundred piculs;
translations.idiomatic: middle-sized units had a chief at four hundred piculs;

sentences.zh: 侯国之相，秩次亦如之。

translations.literal: the chancellors of marquisates followed the same salary ladder.
translations.idiomatic: chancellors of marquisates were paid on the same stepped scale.

sentences.zh: 本注曰：皆掌治民，显善劝义，禁奸罚恶，理讼平贼，恤民时务，秋冬集课，上计于所属郡国。

translations.literal: The original commentary says: All governed the people, displayed good and urged right conduct, forbade evil and punished wickedness, settled lawsuits and suppressed banditry, cared for the people’s seasonal tasks, gathered assessments in autumn and winter, and sent annual accounts up to the supervising commandery or kingdom.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: These officials governed the people, honored virtue, curbed vice, heard cases, kept the peace, timed corvée and taxes to the seasons, held autumn and winter reviews, and forwarded accounts to the parent commandery or kingdom.

sentences.zh: 凡县主蛮夷曰道。

translations.literal: In general counties that chiefly held barbarians were called circuits.
translations.idiomatic: Counties whose population was chiefly non-Chinese were termed circuits.

sentences.zh: 公主所食汤沐曰邑。

translations.literal: Bathing towns granted to princesses were called towns.
translations.idiomatic: Revenue manors bestowed on princesses were called noble towns.

sentences.zh: 县万户以上为令，不满为长。

translations.literal: Counties of ten thousand households or more had magistrates; those below had chiefs.
translations.idiomatic: Units with ten thousand households or more rated a magistrate; smaller ones had a chief.

sentences.zh: 侯国为相。

translations.literal: Marquisates had chancellors.
translations.idiomatic: Marquisates were administered by chancellors.

sentences.zh: 皆秦制也。

translations.literal: All were Qin institutions.
translations.idiomatic: These arrangements descended from Qin practice.

sentences.zh: 丞各一人。

translations.literal: Each had one assistant.
translations.idiomatic: Each county-level unit had one assistant magistrate.

sentences.zh: 尉大县二人，小县一人。

translations.literal: Large counties had two commandants, small counties one.
translations.idiomatic: Populous counties fielded two police commandants; smaller ones had one.

sentences.zh: 本注曰：丞署文书。

translations.literal: The original commentary says: The assistant managed documents.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: The assistant supervised paperwork.

sentences.zh: 典知仓狱。

translations.literal: He was in charge of granaries and prisons.
translations.idiomatic: He oversaw granaries and jails.

sentences.zh: 尉主盗贼。

translations.literal: The commandant was in charge of bandits.
translations.idiomatic: The commandant handled theft and robbery.

sentences.zh: 凡有贼发，主名不立，则推索行寻，案察奸宄，以起端绪。

translations.literal: Whenever a crime occurred and the culprit’s identity was unknown, he pursued leads, investigated hidden evil, and opened the trail.
translations.idiomatic: When a crime lacked a named perpetrator, he followed clues, rooted out accomplices, and opened the investigation.

sentences.zh: 各署诸曹掾史。

translations.literal: Each established various bureau clerks and secretaries.
translations.idiomatic: Each county likewise staffed bureau clerks and secretaries.

sentences.zh: 本注曰：诸曹略如郡员，五官为廷掾，监乡五部，春夏为劝农掾，秋冬为制度掾。

translations.literal: The original commentary says: The bureaus were roughly like those of a commandery; the steward of the five bureaus was the court clerk, supervising five rural districts; in spring and summer he was the clerk for encouraging agriculture, in autumn and winter the clerk for statutes.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: County bureaus echoed commandery models; the steward of the five bureaus doubled as court clerk over five rural circuits, shifting in warm months to agricultural promotion and in cold months to legal compliance.

sentences.zh: 乡置有秩、三老、游徼。

translations.literal: In each township there were salaried elders, three elders, and patrol officers.
translations.idiomatic: Each township appointed a salaried headman, three moral elders, and roving patrol officers.

sentences.zh: 本注曰：有秩，郡所署，秩百石，掌一乡人；

translations.literal: The original commentary says: The salaried headman was appointed by the commandery at one hundred piculs and governed one township’s people;
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: The salaried headman, named by the commandery at one hundred piculs, directed a whole township;

sentences.zh: 其乡小者，县置啬夫一人。

translations.literal: in small townships the county placed one bailiff.
translations.idiomatic: very small townships made do with a single county-appointed bailiff.

sentences.zh: 皆主知民善恶，为役先后，知民贫富，为赋多少，平其差品。

translations.literal: All were to know the people’s good and evil, the order of labor service, the people’s wealth and poverty, and the amount of tax, and to equalize grades of assessment.
translations.idiomatic: They were to know who was virtuous or vicious, who should serve corvée first or last, who was rich or poor, how much tax each owed, and to keep assessments fair.

sentences.zh: 三老掌教化。

translations.literal: The three elders were in charge of moral instruction.
translations.idiomatic: The three elders led moral education.

sentences.zh: 凡有孝子顺孙，贞女义妇，让财救患，及学士为民法式者，皆扁表其门，以兴善行。

translations.literal: Whenever there were filial sons, obedient grandsons, chaste wives, righteous women, those who yielded property or saved others in distress, and scholars who could model conduct for the people, their gates were inscribed to encourage good deeds.
translations.idiomatic: Filial children, chaste widows, donors, rescuers, and scholars who set an example had commendatory plaques hung on their gates to inspire the community.

sentences.zh: 游徼掌徼循，禁司奸盗。

translations.literal: Patrol officers were in charge of patrols and prohibiting spying, theft, and robbery.
translations.idiomatic: Patrol officers patrolled the countryside and suppressed spies, thieves, and robbers.

sentences.zh: 又有乡佐，属乡，主民收赋税。

translations.literal: There were also township aides attached to the township in charge of collecting taxes from the people.
translations.idiomatic: Township aides assisted with tax collection.

sentences.zh: 亭有亭长，以禁盗贼。

translations.literal: Each ward post had a ward head to prohibit bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Every roadside ward had a ward head whose duty was to suppress banditry.

sentences.zh: 本注曰：亭长，主求捕盗贼，承望都尉。

translations.literal: The original commentary says: The ward head was in charge of seeking and capturing bandits and answering to the commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: Ward heads tracked down thieves and reported to the county commandant.

sentences.zh: 里有里魁，民有什伍，善恶以告。

translations.literal: In each hamlet there was a hamlet chief; the people were grouped in tens and fives, and good and evil were reported.
translations.idiomatic: Each hamlet had a chief; households were grouped in tens and fives so that conduct could be reported upward.

sentences.zh: 本注曰：里魁掌一里百家。

translations.literal: The original commentary says: The hamlet chief governed one hamlet of a hundred families.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: A hamlet chief oversaw roughly one hundred households.

sentences.zh: 什主十家，伍主五家，以相检察。

translations.literal: The ten-chief governed ten families, the five-chief five families, mutually inspecting one another.
translations.idiomatic: Leaders of ten and five households watched one another in a mutual-surveillance grid.

sentences.zh: 民有善事恶事，以告监官。

translations.literal: When the people had good or evil deeds, they reported them to the supervising official.
translations.idiomatic: Good or bad behavior was relayed to the supervising magistrate.

sentences.zh: 边县有障塞尉。

translations.literal: Border counties had barrier-and-pass commandants.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier counties posted commandants for barriers and passes.

sentences.zh: 本注曰：掌禁备羌夷犯塞。

translations.literal: The original commentary says: They were in charge of prohibitions and readiness against Qiang and Yi raiding the passes.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: They guarded against Qiang and Yi incursions through the frontier defenses.

sentences.zh: 其郡有盐官、铁官、工官、都水官者，随事广狭置令、长及丞，秩次皆如县、道，无分士，给均本吏。

translations.literal: In commanderies that had salt offices, iron offices, craft offices, or capital-construction water offices, according to the size of the task they placed magistrates, chiefs, and assistants; the salary grades were all like counties and circuits; there was no separate territorial jurisdiction; clerks were supplied evenly from the regular establishment.
translations.idiomatic: Commanderies rich in salt, iron, crafts, or waterworks set magistrates, chiefs, and assistants scaled to the workload, paid like county officials, without an independent territory, drawing clerks from the standard pool.

sentences.zh: 本注曰：凡郡县出盐多者置盐官，主盐税。

translations.literal: The original commentary says: In general commanderies and counties that produced much salt set salt offices in charge of salt tax.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: Salty regions established salt bureaus to levy salt duties.

sentences.zh: 出铁多者置铁官，主鼓铸。

translations.literal: Those that produced much iron set iron offices in charge of smelting and casting.
translations.idiomatic: Iron-rich areas placed iron bureaus to oversee smelting and minting.

sentences.zh: 有工多者置工官，主工税物。

translations.literal: Those with much craftwork set craft offices in charge of craft taxes and goods.
translations.idiomatic: Industrial centers added craft bureaus to tax manufactures.

sentences.zh: 有水池及鱼利多者置水官，主平水收渔税。

translations.literal: Those with ponds and much fish profit set water offices in charge of leveling water and collecting fishing tax.
translations.idiomatic: Where ponds and fisheries flourished, water bureaus regulated irrigation works and fishing levies.

sentences.zh: 在所诸县均差吏更给之。

translations.literal: In the relevant counties clerks were rotated in assignment to supply them.
translations.idiomatic: Clerk labor was rotated among nearby counties to staff these offices.

sentences.zh: 置吏随事，不具县员。

translations.literal: Clerks were placed according to the task and were not counted in the county’s regular quota.
translations.idiomatic: Such posts were ad hoc and did not count toward the county’s authorized headcount.

sentences.zh: 使匈奴中郎将一人，比二千石。

translations.literal: One Herald to the Xiongnu, comparable to two thousand piculs.
translations.idiomatic: A single Herald to the Xiongnu held rank comparable to two thousand piculs.

sentences.zh: 本注曰：主护南单于。

translations.literal: The original commentary says: In charge of protecting the Southern Shanyu.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: He guarded the interests of the Southern Shanyu’s court.

sentences.zh: 置从事二人，有事随事增之，掾随事为员。

translations.literal: Two attendants were established; when there was business they were increased according to the matter; clerks were appointed as needed for the task.
translations.idiomatic: Two staff attendants were standard; extra aides and clerks were added when duties required.

sentences.zh: 护羌、乌桓校尉所置亦然。

translations.literal: The establishment of the Protectors of the Qiang and Wuhuan was the same.
translations.idiomatic: The Protectors of the Qiang and Wuhuan were organized on the same pattern.

sentences.zh: 护乌桓校尉一人，比二千石。

translations.literal: One Protector of the Wuhuan, comparable to two thousand piculs.
translations.idiomatic: One Protector of the Wuhuan held rank comparable to two thousand piculs.

sentences.zh: 本注曰：主乌桓胡。

translations.literal: The original commentary says: In charge of the Wuhuan Hu.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: He supervised the Wuhuan tribes on the northern frontier.

sentences.zh: 护羌校尉一人，比二千石。

translations.literal: One Protector of the Qiang, comparable to two thousand piculs.
translations.idiomatic: One Protector of the Qiang held rank comparable to two thousand piculs.

sentences.zh: 本注曰：主西羌。

translations.literal: The original commentary says: In charge of the Western Qiang.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: His brief covered the western Qiang peoples.

sentences.zh: 皇子封王，其郡为国，每置傅一人，相一人，皆二千石。

translations.literal: When imperial sons were enfeoffed as kings, their commanderies became kingdoms; each had one tutor and one chancellor, both at two thousand piculs.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial princes received kingdoms built on commanderies, each staffed with a tutor and a chancellor at two thousand piculs.

sentences.zh: 本注曰：傅主导王以善，礼如师，不臣也。

translations.literal: The original commentary says: The tutor guided the king toward goodness with ritual like a teacher and was not treated as a subject.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: The tutor instructed the prince in virtue with the deference due a teacher rather than a minister.

sentences.zh: 相如太守。

translations.literal: The chancellor was like a grand administrator.
translations.idiomatic: The kingdom chancellor corresponded to a commandery grand administrator.

sentences.zh: 其长史，如郡丞。

translations.literal: Its chief clerk was like a commandery assistant.
translations.idiomatic: The kingdom chief clerk matched a commandery assistant magistrate.

sentences.zh: 汉初立诸王，因项羽所立诸王之制，地既广大，且至千里。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Han, when the various kings were established, they followed the system of kings set up by Xiang Yu; the territory was vast, reaching as much as a thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: Early Han princes inherited Xiang Yu’s sprawling kingdoms, some stretching a thousand li across.

sentences.zh: 又其官职，傅为太傅，相为丞相，又有御史大夫及诸卿，皆秩二千石，百官皆如朝廷。

translations.literal: Moreover their offices: the tutor was grand tutor, the chancellor was chancellor of state, and there were also imperial clerks and the various ministers, all at two thousand piculs, the hundred officials all like the court.
translations.idiomatic: Their governments copied the capital: grand tutor, chancellor of state, censor-in-chief, and ministers at two thousand piculs—a full court in miniature.

sentences.zh: 国家唯为置丞相，其御史大夫以下皆自置之。

translations.literal: The state only set up the chancellor for them; from the censor-in-chief downward they appointed themselves.
translations.idiomatic: The central government named only the chancellor; princes chose their own censor-in-chief and subordinates.

sentences.zh: 至景帝时，吴、楚七国恃其国大，遂以作乱，几危汉室。

translations.literal: By Emperor Jing’s time, the seven kingdoms of Wu and Chu relied on their great size and then rebelled, nearly endangering the Han house.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Jing the great kingdoms of Wu and Chu rose in revolt and nearly toppled the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 及其诛灭，景帝惩之，遂令诸王不得治民，令内史主治民，改丞相曰相，省御史大夫、廷尉、少府、宗正、博士官。

translations.literal: When they were exterminated, Emperor Jing took warning and ordered the kings not to govern the people, ordered interior clerks to govern the people instead, changed the chancellor of state to chancellor, and abolished the posts of censor-in-chief, commandant of justice, privy treasurer, director of the imperial clan, and erudits.
translations.idiomatic: After their defeat Emperor Jing stripped princes of civil authority, transferred rule to imperial clerks, downgraded the chief minister to “chancellor,” and eliminated replica ministries such as justice, finance, clan affairs, and the academy.

sentences.zh: 武帝改汉内史、中尉、郎中令之名，而王国如故，员职皆朝廷为署，不得自置。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu changed the Han names of interior clerk, commandant of the capital, and chamberlain for the palace guard, but the kingdoms remained as before; all posts were appointed by the court and could not be self-appointed.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu renamed the kingdom interior clerk, capital commandant, and chamberlain for the guard to match Han titles, yet appointments for every office now came from the center, not the prince.

sentences.zh: 至成帝省内史治民，更令相治民，太傅但曰傅。

translations.literal: By Emperor Cheng the interior clerk who governed the people was abolished and the chancellor was ordered to govern the people instead; the grand tutor was simply called tutor.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Cheng abolished the kingdom interior clerk and transferred civil government to the chancellor, while the grand tutor was shortened to “tutor.”

sentences.zh: 中尉一人，比二千石。

translations.literal: One commandant of the capital for the kingdom, comparable to two thousand piculs.
translations.idiomatic: Each kingdom appointed one capital commandant at rank comparable to two thousand piculs.

sentences.zh: 本注曰：职如郡都尉，主盗贼。

translations.literal: The original commentary says: The duties were like those of a commandery commandant; he was in charge of bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: His portfolio matched a commandery commandant’s, with chief responsibility for theft and robbery.

sentences.zh: 郎中令一人，仆一人，皆千石。

translations.literal: One chamberlain for the palace guard and one steward, both at one thousand piculs.
translations.idiomatic: The household included one chamberlain for the palace guard and one steward of chariots, each at one thousand piculs.

sentences.zh: 本注曰：郎中令掌王大夫、郎中宿卫，官如光禄勋。

translations.literal: The original commentary says: The chamberlain for the palace guard supervised the king’s grandees and gentleman attendants on night guard; the office was like the Chamberlain for the Palace Revenues.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: The chamberlain commanded the king’s senior retainers and rotating gentleman guards, on the model of the metropolitan Chamberlain for the Palace Revenues.

sentences.zh: 自省少府，职皆并焉。

translations.literal: From the privy treasurer downward all functions were merged into it.
translations.idiomatic: From the privy treasurer on down, those duties were folded into his office.

sentences.zh: 仆主车及驭，如太仆。

translations.literal: The steward was in charge of chariots and driving, like the grand coachman.
translations.idiomatic: The steward managed carriages and teams, paralleling the grand coachman at court.

sentences.zh: 本曰太仆，比二千石，武帝改，但曰仆，又皆减其秩。

translations.literal: Originally called grand coachman, comparable to two thousand piculs; Emperor Wu changed it to simply steward, and also reduced all their ranks.
translations.idiomatic: The post had been the grand coachman at “comparable to two thousand piculs”; Emperor Wu shortened the title to steward and cut the salary grades across the board.

sentences.zh: 治书，比六百石。

translations.literal: Document clerks, comparable to six hundred piculs.
translations.idiomatic: Kingdom document clerks held rank comparable to six hundred piculs.

sentences.zh: 本注曰：治书本尚书更名。

translations.literal: The original commentary says: Document clerks were the former masters of writing of the palace secretary, renamed.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: They were the old “masters of writing” staff of the imperial secretary, retitled for service in a princely household.

sentences.zh: 大夫，比六百石。

translations.literal: Grandees, comparable to six hundred piculs.
translations.idiomatic: Household grandees ranked at six hundred piculs.

sentences.zh: 本注曰：无员。

translations.literal: The original commentary says: No fixed quota.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: There was no statutory headcount.

sentences.zh: 掌奉王使至京都，奉璧贺正月，及使诸国。

translations.literal: They bore the king’s missions to the capital, presented the jade disc to congratulate on the first month, and were dispatched to other states.
translations.idiomatic: They carried the prince’s embassies to the capital, presented the congratulatory jade token at New Year audiences, and traveled on mission to other kingdoms.

sentences.zh: 本皆持节，后去节。

translations.literal: Originally all carried staffs of authority; later the staff was removed.
translations.idiomatic: At first they carried credentialed staffs; later that emblem was dropped.

sentences.zh: 谒者，比四百石。

translations.literal: Ushers, comparable to four hundred piculs.
translations.idiomatic: Ushers were graded at four hundred piculs.

sentences.zh: 本注曰：掌冠长冠。

translations.literal: The original commentary says: In charge of the king’s formal cap and long court cap.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: They guarded the ritual regalia—the capping cap and the long court headdress—used when the king received investiture or held court.

sentences.zh: 本员十六人，后减。

translations.literal: Originally the establishment was sixteen men; later it was reduced.
translations.idiomatic: The corps once numbered sixteen; later it was trimmed.

sentences.zh: 礼乐长。

translations.literal: Director of ritual and music.
translations.idiomatic: A director of ritual and music headed the princely orchestra and ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 本注曰：主乐人。

translations.literal: The original commentary says: In charge of musicians.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: He supervised the household musicians.

sentences.zh: 卫士长。

translations.literal: Captain of the guardsmen.
translations.idiomatic: A captain of the guardsmen commanded the standing watch.

sentences.zh: 本注曰：主卫士。

translations.literal: The original commentary says: In charge of the guardsmen.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: He led the palace guard contingent.

sentences.zh: 医工长。

translations.literal: Chief of physicians.
translations.idiomatic: A chief physician oversaw the medical staff.

sentences.zh: 本注曰：主医药。

translations.literal: The original commentary says: In charge of medicine.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: He managed drugs and treatment for the household.

sentences.zh: 永巷长。

translations.literal: Warden of the everlasting lane.
translations.idiomatic: A warden of the “everlasting lane” policed the inner quarters’ corridors.

sentences.zh: 本注曰：宦者，主宫中婢使。

translations.literal: The original commentary says: A eunuch; in charge of palace maids and serving women.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: The post was held by a eunuch who directed maidservants in the harem wing.

sentences.zh: 祠祀长。

translations.literal: Director of sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: A director of sacrifices arranged the princely ancestral rites.

sentences.zh: 本注曰：主祠祀。

translations.literal: The original commentary says: In charge of sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: He handled offerings at the princely shrines.

sentences.zh: 皆比四百石。

translations.literal: All were comparable to four hundred piculs.
translations.idiomatic: These specialist heads all drew pay comparable to four hundred piculs.

sentences.zh: 郎中，二百石。

translations.literal: Gentlemen attendants, two hundred piculs.
translations.idiomatic: Gentlemen of the household guard stood at two hundred piculs.

sentences.zh: 本注曰：无员。

translations.literal: The original commentary says: No fixed quota.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: Their numbers were not fixed by statute.

sentences.zh: 卫公、宋公。

translations.literal: The Dukes of Wei and Song.
translations.idiomatic: The chapter next treats the Dukes of Wei and Song, fiefs honoring the ancient dynastic lines.

sentences.zh: 本注曰：建武二年，封周后姬常为周承休公；

translations.literal: The original commentary says: In the second year of Jianwu he enfeoffed Ji Chang, a descendant of the Zhou, as Duke Who Continues the Blessings of Zhou;
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: In Jianwu 2 the emperor enfeoffed Ji Chang, heir of the Zhou royal house, as duke charged with continuing Zhou’s blessing;

sentences.zh: 五年，封殷后孔安为殷绍嘉公。

translations.literal: in the fifth year he enfeoffed Kong An, a descendant of Yin, as Duke Who Connects the Luster of Yin.
translations.idiomatic: in Jianwu 5 he enfeoffed Kong An, scion of the Yin (Shang) line, as duke tasked with linking Yin’s residual glory to the Han.

sentences.zh: 十三年，改常为卫公，安为宋公，以为汉宾，在三公上。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he changed Chang to Duke of Wei and An to Duke of Song, making them guest-lords of the Han, ranked above the three excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianwu 13 Ji Chang became Duke of Wei and Kong An Duke of Song, honored as ritual “guests” of the Han and seated above the three excellencies.

sentences.zh: 列侯，所食县为侯国。

translations.literal: Full marquises: the county from which they drew income became a marquisate.
translations.idiomatic: A full marquis took his stipendiary county as his marquisate.

sentences.zh: 本注曰：承秦爵二十等，为彻侯，金印紫绶，以赏有功。

translations.literal: The original commentary says: Continuing the Qin system of twenty ranks, they were complete marquises with gold seal and purple ribbon, to reward merit.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: The rank continued the Qin twentieth grade—the complete marquis—with gold seal and purple cord, as the highest reward for service.

sentences.zh: 功大者食县，小者食乡、亭，得臣其所食吏民。

translations.literal: Those of great merit fed from a whole county; the lesser fed from a township or ward, and were allowed to treat the clerks and people they fed from as subjects.
translations.idiomatic: The greatest meritorious lords drew an entire county; lesser ones drew only a township or a ward, and might treat the households within that endowment as personal dependents.

sentences.zh: 后避武帝讳，为列侯。

translations.literal: Later, to avoid Emperor Wu’s taboo, they were called full marquises.
translations.idiomatic: Later the title was softened to “full marquis” to avoid the taboo on Emperor Wu’s personal name (from “complete” marquis).

sentences.zh: 武帝元朔二年，令诸王得推恩分众子土，国家为封，亦为列侯。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuanshuo Emperor Wu ordered the kings to extend favor and divide land among their many sons; the state enfeoffed them, and they too became full marquises.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanshuo 2 Emperor Wu allowed kings to “extend favor” by subdividing domains for younger sons; the court packaged those parcels as full marquisates.

sentences.zh: 旧列侯奉朝请在长安者，位次三公。

translations.literal: Formerly full marquises who attended court and awaited summons in Chang’an ranked just below the three excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, full marquises who maintained residences in Chang’an and answered periodic court summons stood immediately beneath the three excellencies in order of precedence.

sentences.zh: 中兴以来，唯以功德赐位特进者，次军骑将军；

translations.literal: Since the restoration only those granted specially advanced rank for merit ranked next after the general-in-chief who commanded cavalry and chariots;
translations.idiomatic: After the restoration only nobles honored with the “specially advanced” grade for outstanding merit ranked next after the general-in-chief of chariots and cavalry;

sentences.zh: 赐位朝侯，次五校尉；

translations.literal: those granted the rank of court marquis ranked next after the five colonels;
translations.idiomatic: those given the courtesy rank of “court marquis” followed the five colonels of the guard;

sentences.zh: 赐位侍祠侯，次大夫。

translations.literal: those granted the rank of attendant-sacrifice marquis ranked next after grandees.
translations.idiomatic: and holders of the “attendant-sacrifice marquis” designation stood just after ordinary grandees.

sentences.zh: 其余以BD4A附及公主子孙奉坟墓于京都者，亦随时见会，位在博士、议郎下。

translations.literal: The rest—imperial clansmen in close attendance at court, together with descendants of princesses who maintained tombs in the capital—also attended assemblies from time to time, ranked below erudits and consultants.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone else—cadet imperial kinsmen who stayed at court by privilege, plus descendants of princesses assigned to tend imperial tombs in the capital—might be summoned to selected audiences, always seated below the erudits and advisory gentlemen.

sentences.zh: 诸王封者受茅土，归以立社稷，礼也。

translations.literal: Those princes who received investiture took the clods of earth with hemp and reeds home to establish the altars of soil and grain; it was proper ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Enfeoffed kings carried the clod of sacred soil with its tuft of ritual grass back to their capitals to found the altars of soil and grain, as canonical rite prescribed.

sentences.zh: 列土、特进、朝侯贺正月执璧云。

translations.literal: Full marquises, specially advanced nobles, and court marquises likewise, when congratulating on the first month, held jade discs.
translations.idiomatic: Full marquises, specially advanced peers, and court marquises presented jade tokens at the New Year audience in the same fashion.

sentences.zh: 每国置相一人，其秩各如本县。

translations.literal: Each marquisate placed one chancellor; his salary grade matched the original county.
translations.idiomatic: Every marquisate had a single chancellor whose pay scale matched the underlying county’s rank.

sentences.zh: 本注曰：主治民，如令、长，不臣也。

translations.literal: The original commentary says: He governed the people like a magistrate or chief but was not treated as the marquis’s subject minister.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: He ruled commoners exactly as a county magistrate would, yet he was not the marquis’s vassal minister—he answered to the throne.

sentences.zh: 但纳租于侯，以户数为限。

translations.literal: They only paid rent to the marquis according to household numbers as the limit.
translations.idiomatic: Tenant households forwarded only the contracted rent to the marquis, capped by registered household counts.

sentences.zh: 其家臣，置家丞、庶子各一人。

translations.literal: For household ministers they placed one household aide and one junior son-of-the-house.
translations.idiomatic: Domestic administration relied on one household aide and one junior steward of the house.

sentences.zh: 本注曰：主侍侯，使理家事。

translations.literal: The original commentary says: They attended the marquis and managed household affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: These officers served the marquis personally and ran his private establishment.

sentences.zh: 列侯旧有行人、洗马、门大夫，凡五官。

translations.literal: Formerly full marquises had heralds, horse washers, and gate grandees—five offices in all.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old system a full marquis kept heralds, outriders who washed the horses at halts, and gate grandees—five household ministries altogether.

sentences.zh: 中兴以来，食邑千户已上置家丞、庶子各一人，不满千户不置家丞，又悉省行人、洗马、门大夫。

translations.literal: Since the restoration, for feoffs of one thousand households or more they placed one household aide and one junior son-of-the-house; below one thousand households they did not place a household aide, and they abolished heralds, horse washers, and gate grandees entirely.
translations.idiomatic: After the restoration, marquises with at least one thousand feoffed households retained an aide and a junior steward; smaller feoffs lost the household aide, and heralds, washers, and gate grandees were cut altogether.

sentences.zh: 关内侯，承秦赐爵十九等，为关内侯，无土，寄食在所县，民租多少，各有户数为限。

translations.literal: Marquis-within-the-passes continued the Qin nineteenth rank as marquis-within-the-passes; they had no territory but lodged grain income in a given county, the people’s rent being limited according to household numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Marquises-within-the-passes inherited the Qin nineteenth-grade title: they held no land but drew a cash-and-grain allowance charged against a host county, with yields prorated to the number of registered households.

sentences.zh: 四夷国王，率众王，归义侯，邑君，邑长，皆有丞，比郡、县。

translations.literal: Kings of the four quarters, chieftains-at-heads-of-crowds, marquises who had submitted in righteousness, town lords, and town chiefs all had assistants, comparable to commanderies and counties.
translations.idiomatic: Tributary kings, tribal “chiefs who lead hosts,” marquises of submission, town lords, and town chiefs each received deputy officers modeled on commandery and county assistants.

sentences.zh: 百官受奉例：大将军、三公奉，月三百五十斛。

translations.literal: Examples of official stipends: the grand general and the three excellencies received three hundred fifty hu per month.
translations.idiomatic: Stipends were reckoned in grain: the grand general and the three excellencies drew three hundred fifty hu a month.

sentences.zh: 中二千石奉，月百八十斛。

translations.literal: For fully two thousand piculs the stipend was one hundred eighty hu per month.
translations.idiomatic: Officials at the “full two thousand picul” grade received one hundred eighty hu monthly.

sentences.zh: 二千石奉，月百二十斛。

translations.literal: For two thousand piculs the stipend was one hundred twenty hu per month.
translations.idiomatic: A straight two-thousand-picul salary meant one hundred twenty hu each month.

sentences.zh: 比二千石奉，月百斛。

translations.literal: For comparable to two thousand piculs the stipend was one hundred hu per month.
translations.idiomatic: The “comparable to two thousand piculs” band paid one hundred hu.

sentences.zh: 千石奉，月八十斛。

translations.literal: For one thousand piculs the stipend was eighty hu per month.
translations.idiomatic: One-thousand-picul posts drew eighty hu.

sentences.zh: 六百石奉，月七十斛。

translations.literal: For six hundred piculs the stipend was seventy hu per month.
translations.idiomatic: Six-hundred-picul officials took seventy hu.

sentences.zh: 比六百石奉，月五十斛。

translations.literal: For comparable to six hundred piculs the stipend was fifty hu per month.
translations.idiomatic: The “comparable to six hundred” grade received fifty hu.

sentences.zh: 四百石奉，月四十五斛。

translations.literal: For four hundred piculs the stipend was forty-five hu per month.
translations.idiomatic: Four-hundred-picul salaries came to forty-five hu.

sentences.zh: 比四百石奉，月四十斛。

translations.literal: For comparable to four hundred piculs the stipend was forty hu per month.
translations.idiomatic: “Comparable to four hundred” meant forty hu.

sentences.zh: 三百石奉，月四十斛。

translations.literal: For three hundred piculs the stipend was forty hu per month.
translations.idiomatic: Three-hundred-picul posts oddly matched forty hu as well.

sentences.zh: 比三百石奉，月三十七斛。

translations.literal: For comparable to three hundred piculs the stipend was thirty-seven hu per month.
translations.idiomatic: “Comparable to three hundred” paid thirty-seven hu.

sentences.zh: 二百石奉，月三十斛。

translations.literal: For two hundred piculs the stipend was thirty hu per month.
translations.idiomatic: Two-hundred-picul clerks drew thirty hu.

sentences.zh: 比二百石奉，月二十七斛。

translations.literal: For comparable to two hundred piculs the stipend was twenty-seven hu per month.
translations.idiomatic: “Comparable to two hundred” meant twenty-seven hu.

sentences.zh: 一百石奉，月十六斛。

translations.literal: For one hundred piculs the stipend was sixteen hu per month.
translations.idiomatic: One-hundred-picul minor officials received sixteen hu.

sentences.zh: 斗食奉，月十一斛。

translations.literal: For “dou-food” clerks the stipend was eleven hu per month.
translations.idiomatic: “Dou-food” subclerks—paid by the peck—took eleven hu monthly.

sentences.zh: 佐史奉，月八斛。

translations.literal: For assistant clerks the stipend was eight hu per month.
translations.idiomatic: Assistant clerks at the bottom of the scale drew eight hu.

sentences.zh: 凡诸受奉，皆半钱半谷。

translations.literal: In general all who received stipends received half in cash and half in grain.
translations.idiomatic: Every grade on the schedule was normally split half in coin and half in unhusked grain.

sentences.zh: 赞曰：帝道渊默，冢帅修德。

translations.literal: The eulogy says: The imperial way is deep and silent; the high ministers at the ancestral shrine cultivate virtue.
translations.idiomatic: The summation reads: The royal path runs silent and deep; the chief ministers who stand at the high altar polish their virtue.

sentences.zh: 寡以御众，分职乃克。

translations.literal: With few principles he governed the many; only when offices were divided could it succeed.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler guides the multitude through restraint; order comes only when every office keeps its brief.

sentences.zh: 不置不监，无骄无忒。

translations.literal: What is not set up is not supervised; there is neither arrogance nor transgression.
translations.idiomatic: Leave unneeded posts unfilled and they need no overseers—then there is neither swagger among officials nor dereliction of duty.

sentences.zh: 程是师徒，宁民康国。

translations.literal: Take these masters and disciples as your model, and the people are quieted and the state is at peace.
translations.idiomatic: Hold this cadre of teachers and followers to the standard, and the common people find rest while the realm flourishes in peace.
